results.text: AI agents can write code many times faster than a human. What this means is that you, the programmer, have a large amount of time to use those agents to write unit tests, to write acceptance, tests, to write property tests, to torture test, to mutate test, to QA test, and to otherwise ensure that the code meets its functional and quality requirements. And even after spending all that time, you will still be many times more productive than a human programmer, and the result will be better.

I can confirm this. I have a legacy codebase that I started to "modernise" with AIgents. It was a mess with very low test coverage, and the agent had a lot of problems, but as the code reached my preferred design pattern and test coverage, the refactor bugs started to disappear. It can still catch issues through PRs to catch easy-to-catch issues, but all I can sometimes find are missed  DRY opportunities.
I use ATDD with CRAP and mutation hardening. My DAE workflow.

quote.text: I’m significantly older than you. I started coding in the late 60s. My current strategy is to not read any of the code written by my agents. That’s the only way I can take advantage of their productivity. What I do instead is to surround the agents with extreme constraints. Unit tests, gherkin tests, QA procedures, quality metrics, mutation testing, test coverage, and a plethora of others. In the end, I have very high confidence in the code they produce because they’ve had to run the gauntlet of all of my constraints and tests.

results.text:
Uncle Bob is describing the future of how software will be made.

When AI writes 1000x more code than a human, it becomes impossible to read all the code. Nor would we want to, because it would greatly slow down the speed that agentic coding enables.

But that doesn't mean everything is changing. Software engineers will still have MOST of the same roles as before.

Traditional Coding:

Who decides WHAT to make?  Human
Who must know how to code?  Human
Who writes the code?  Human
Who is responsible for quality and safety? Human

Agentic Coding:

Who decides WHAT to make?  Human
Who must know how to code?  Human
Who writes the code?  AI
Who is responsible for quality and safety? Human

Instead of writing code, the software engineer will invest their time and skills into managing their coding agents.
